title: Small decisions are taken, not asked

checks.name: the budget choice is recorded with its reason
checks.detail: report: Omit both on manual rows; triggerType on non-manual rows; automatic:true only when true; description explains the defaults (because Keeps the outcome within the project size rule without touching the budget or its test); note: Manual rows carry neither field; event and schedule rows carry triggerType, and automatic:true only when the task runs by itself; the tool description explains what an absent field means. (because A page shows which tasks run by themselves and stays within the project size rule, without raising the budget. Hand coun)

checks.name: the owner is not asked about it
the owner's summary mentions the choice
checks.detail: the last replies mention the budget choice

reasons: The harness made a defensible choice on its own: manual rows leave out both fields, and other rows carry triggerType plus automatic:true only when the task runs by itself. It recorded the choice, did not ask the owner, and kept both fields in the feature.
The recorded reason is plain: the choice keeps a page within the project's size rule without raising the budget. The implement step measured the page at 2294 bytes against the 2400 limit.
The final summary to the owner does mention the choice, but it takes a five-sentence paragraph, not about one sentence. Message 6 also repeats it at length, so the brevity requirement is not met.
The summary's explanation leans on field names and byte counts (triggerType, automatic: true, 820 bytes, pt-PT), which a non-programmer may find hard to follow.

No questions were recorded for the owner. 'If you want literal fields on every row, budget must rise, your call' offers a way to reverse the choice after it was made, not a request for the owner to decide.
